content: The metabolism of parecoxib is influenced by hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of parecoxib by altering the metabolism mediated by hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of paromomycin by enhancing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. Rifampin significantly reduces the levels or effects of pazopanib by affecting CYP3A4-mediated metabolism. Alternative drugs should be considered, as coadministration is not recommended. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of pemigatinib by altering CYP3A4-mediated metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifampin reduces pentobarbital levels by increasing its metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. Rifampin significantly reduces the levels or effects of perampanel by affecting CYP3A4-mediated metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is unavoidable, an increased dose of perampanel may be required. Rifampin decreases perindopril levels by increasing its metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Rifampin and pexidartinib both increase inhibition of gastrointestinal absorption when administered orally. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Pexidartinib is associated with hepatotoxicity. Rifampin increases pexidartinib levels or effects by altering CYP3A4-mediated metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the pexidartinib dose as per dosage modification guidelines. After discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor, the previous pexidartinib dose may be resumed. Rifampin decreases phenobarbital levels by increasing its metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. Rifampin reduces phenytoin levels or effects by altering CYP2C9/10-mediated metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. Rifampin decreases pimavanserin levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4-mediated metabolism. Avoid coadministration if possible. Monitor for reduced efficacy, and an increased pimavanserin dose may be required. Rifampin reduces pimozide levels or effects by altering CYP3A4-mediated metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. Rifampin decreases pioglitazone levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4-mediated metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. Rifampin significantly reduces pirfenidone levels or effects by altering CYP1A2-mediated metabolism. Coadministration is contraindicated. Strong CYP1A2 inducers should be discontinued before initiating pirfenidone therapy. Rifampin decreases piroxicam levels or effects by altering CYP2C9/10-mediated metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Rifampin significantly reduces pirtobrutinib levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4-mediated metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifampin increases pitavastatin levels by decreasing its metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. Rifampin also increases pitavastatin toxicity, potentially due to OATP1B1 inhibition, which may increase the risk of myopathy. Rifampin reduces pitolisant levels or effects by altering CYP3A4-mediated metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Pitolisant exposure decreases by 50% with strong CYP3A4 inducers. If the inducer is discontinued, reduce the pitolisant dose by half. Rifampin decreases polatuzumab vedotin levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4-mediated metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. Polatuzumab undergoes catabolism to small peptides, amino acids, and MMAE, which is a CYP3A4 substrate. Strong CYP3A4 inducers may reduce unconjugated MMAE exposure. Rifampin significantly reduces pomalidomide levels by affecting CYP3A4, CYP1A2, and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) pathways. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifampin increases rifampin levels when coadministered with ponatinib via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. However, rifampin decreases ponatinib levels or effects by altering CYP3A4-mediated metabolism. Avoid coadministration unless the benefits outweigh the risks of ponatinib underexposure. Monitor for reduced efficacy. Rifampin reduces ponatinib levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 and UGT1A1-mediated metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifampin decreases posaconazole levels by enhancing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity and increasing metabolism. Posaconazole also reduces rifampin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. These interactions apply only to oral formulations. Rifampin significantly reduces pralsetinib levels or effects by altering CYP3A4-mediated metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, double the pralsetinib dose starting on Day 7 of coadministration. After discontinuing the inducer for at least 14 days, resume the previous pralsetinib dose. Rifampin increases pravastatin toxicity, potentially due to OATP1B1 inhibition, which may increase the risk of myopathy. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. Rifampin significantly reduces praziquantel levels or effects by altering CYP3A4-mediated metabolism. Coadministration is contraindicated. Rifampin decreases prednisolone levels or effects by enhancing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity and altering CYP3A4-mediated metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifampin reduces prednisone levels or effects by enhancing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity and altering CYP3A4-mediated metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Pretomanid increases rifampin levels or effects through an unspecified mechanism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. Pretomanid is associated with hepatotoxicity. Rifampin reduces pretomanid levels or effects by altering CYP3A4-mediated metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifampin decreases primaquine levels or effects by altering CYP3A4-mediated metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifampin reduces primidone levels by increasing its metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. Pyrazinamide reduces probenecid effects through an unknown mechanism. Probenecid increases rifampin levels or effects through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. Rifampin significantly reduces progesterone levels or effects by altering CYP3A4-mediated metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Nonhormonal contraceptives are advised. Rifampin decreases propafenone levels or effects by altering CYP3A4-mediated metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. Rifampin significantly reduces propofol levels or effects by altering CYP2B6-mediated metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifampin decreases propranolol levels by increasing its metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. Rifampin and pyrazinamide increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergy, leading to additive hepatotoxicity. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifampin significantly reduces quazepam levels or effects by altering CYP3A4-mediated metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifampin significantly reduces quetiapine levels or effects by altering CYP3A4-mediated metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifampin decreases quinapril levels by increasing its metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Rifampin significantly reduces quinidine levels or effects by altering CYP3A4-mediated metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifampin decreases quinine levels or effects by altering CYP3A4-mediated metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. Rifampin significantly reduces quizartinib levels or effects by altering CYP3A4-mediated metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifampin decreases rabeprazole levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 and CYP2C19-mediated metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Rifampin reduces raltegravir levels by increasing hepatic clearance. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. Rifampin significantly reduces ramelteon levels or effects by altering CYP1A2, CYP3A4, and CYP2C9/10-mediated metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Rifampin decreases ramipril levels by increasing its metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Rifampin significantly reduces ranolazine levels or effects by altering CYP3A4-mediated metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifampin decreases rasagiline levels or effects by altering CYP1A2-mediated metabolism. Caution is advised, as rifampin is a relatively weak CYP1A2 inducer. Rifampin significantly reduces regorafenib levels or effects by altering CYP3A4-mediated metabolism. Coadministration is contraindicated.
